decision: How should WF-121 reuse the per-page dwell rules and the CRM engagement vocabulary that already exist, instead of re-declaring them?

state.requirement: The build brief says: discover the WF-006, WF-018 and WF-042 domain packages and reuse their dwell and CRM vocabulary instead of re-declaring it. The hard rule also says a domain module imports nothing but the store, and never dsr.api or a bare sqlite3 connection.

existing_domain_packages.dsr.pdf_analytics: WF-018 per-page dwell. Exposes group_sessions (session/revisit split on SESSION_GAP_SECONDS), dwell_per_page, drop_off_per_page, SESSION_GAP_SECONDS=1800, as_seconds, parse_ts. Imports only dsr.store.
existing_domain_packages.dsr.crm_engagement: WF-037 CRM engagement write-back. Exposes CANONICAL_FIELDS (type, occurred_at, asset, dwell_seconds, buyer_email, buyer_crm_id), FIELD_SYNONYMS, and EngagementSync.record_event which records a local engagement row and enqueues a CRM create.
existing_domain_packages.dsr.crm_integration: WF-042 pull of CRM deal, account and contact records into a room; resolves which CRM records a buyer's view belongs to.
existing_domain_packages.dsr.link_gating: WF-069 gate: password, expiry and email verification. Exposes rules.parse_moment, rules.expiry_state (expiry is a boundary: now > expires_at), rules.normalize_email, GateEngine.

state.observed_precedent: Cross-domain imports are already the norm in dsr/<package>/ modules: dsr.fieldmap.vocabulary imports dsr.access; dsr.market_intent.views imports dsr.triage; dsr.chase vocabulary imports dsr.conversation_chase. No guard bans a domain package importing another domain package. The enforced guards ban only dsr.api, dsr.features from a domain package, and sqlite3 in a feature module.
state.risk: Duplicating the session gap, the dwell arithmetic, or the canonical engagement field names would give the same rule two definitions that can drift, which is what the brief says not to do. Putting the shared rules in the HTTP feature module instead of the domain package weakens the domain layer and makes the pure rules harder to test.
state.constraint: Whatever is chosen, the feature module must still expose the reused vocabulary on its /vocabulary route so a reviewer can see the shared values rather than a private copy.

verdict.instructions: Which option best satisfies the brief's reuse requirement while keeping the domain package free of the HTTP app and of a raw sqlite3 connection?

criteria.reuse_in_domain: dsr/tracked_deal_link imports dsr.pdf_analytics and dsr.crm_engagement (and dsr.link_gating rules) directly, so each shared rule has exactly one definition. The package still imports no dsr.api, no fastapi and no sqlite3.
criteria.composition_at_feature: dsr/tracked_deal_link imports only dsr.store; the HTTP feature module imports dsr.pdf_analytics and dsr.crm_engagement and passes the shared constants and metric functions into the domain as parameters.
criteria.duplicate_constants: dsr/tracked_deal_link declares its own copies of the session gap, the dwell arithmetic and the canonical engagement field names and imports no sibling domain package.

why.instructions: What is the strongest reason for the choice?

criteria.single_definition: One definition of each shared rule removes the drift the brief warns about and is testable in the domain layer.
criteria.layer_purity: Keeping the domain package store-only protects a strict reading of the contract at the cost of an injection seam.
criteria.isolation: Avoiding all sibling imports keeps the package independent of other features' code.
